glm.feedback:
## Findings

- **Category:** test
  **Severity:** medium
  **File:** client/src/components/triage/TriageFilterSortBar.test.tsx:12 (`setPhone`)
  **Finding:** The matchMedia mock matches on the exact query string `"(max-width: 767px)"`. If `useIsPhoneViewport()` uses any other formulation (e.g. `(max-width: 767.98px)` or a shared constant that drifts), every phone test silently passes with `matches: false` and the collapsed-by-default behavior is never exercised — the tests would pass against an implementation whose phone branch never fires.
  **Suggestion:** Import the hook's actual media-query constant (or export it) and build the mock from it, so the fence can't silently decouple from the implementation.

- **Category:** edge-case
  **Severity:** low
  **File:** client/src/components/triage/TriageFilterSortBar.tsx (`contentVisible = !isPhone || phoneOpen`)
  **Finding:** On phone, when filters are actively excluding items, the bar collapses to just "Filters & sort" with no indication that filters are applied — users may see a shortened/empty list with no visible cause. Not an AC violation (AC4 says collapsed by default), but a real usability gap for the exact flow AC3/AC4 are optimizing.
  **Suggestion:** Show an active-filter count on the toggle (e.g. "Filters & sort (2)") — cheap, and mirrors the MoreOptionsDisclosure convention already cited.

- **Category:** edge-case
  **Severity:** low
  **File:** client/src/components/external/NewIssueModal/ModalShell.tsx (`max-h-[80dvh]` + `top-[10%]`)
  **Finding:** `top-[10%]` is computed against the small (ICB) viewport while `dvh` tracks the dynamic viewport; on a browser with a tall hidden URL bar, 10% top + 80dvh height can exceed the visible viewport by ~10-70px, clipping the footer again. The spec discloses the vh/dvh mechanism as unverifiable in this harness, but this particular interaction (top-% offset vs dvh cap) is a distinct, unaddressed residual.
  **Suggestion:** Use `top-[10dvh]` (or `max-h-[70dvh]` with the 10% top) so both use the same unit, or cap with `max-h-[min(80dvh,90dv-...)]`. Worth a manual-verification note at minimum.

- **Category:** regression
  **Severity:** low
  **File:** client/src/components/common/ModalScrollBody.tsx (doc change) + any callers not shown
  **Finding:** `max-h-full` only resolves if the immediate parent chain has definite height. The diff updates ModalShell to provide that, but the doc change ("prefer max-h-full") plus the invariant test permitting `max-h-*` generally means a future caller copying the pattern into a non-flex parent will silently get an unbounded body — exactly the production bug this iterate found once already.
  **Suggestion:** Extend the ModalScrollBody doc/invariant to state the hard requirement (parent must be `flex min-h-0` with definite flexed height, itself a flex/grid container for percentage resolution), which is currently only documented in a ModalShell comment.

- **Category:** test
  **Severity:** low
  **File:** client/e2e/flows/mobile-triage-spacing-filters.spec.ts (AC2 test)
  **Finding:** The AC2 test checks left-edge containment against both dialog and viewport but never asserts the right edge against the page viewport (only against the dialog). Since the dialog itself is `max-w-[95vw]`-style positioned, a dialog shifted past the right viewport edge would still pass the dialog-relative assertion. Practically low risk given the dialog's centering.
  **Suggestion:** Add `box.x + box.width <= viewport width` for symmetry.

Non-findings I checked deliberately: the AC3 E2E's isLoading-race fix (waiting on `triage-open-items-*`) is correct and documented; the `flex flex-col` on the body-slot wrapper is a genuine, well-root-caused fix; desktop behavior of the filter bar is provably unchanged (`!isPhone || phoneOpen` → always true at ≥768px); the deferred/per-project margin changes are pure `max-md:` additions with desktop values untouched; the removal of the `calc(100vh-280px)` assertion from ModalShell.test.tsx is consistent with the new class fence in ModalShell.layout.test.tsx, which covers the full chain including the middle links.

## Overall assessment

The change implements all four ACs with an unusually honest test ledger (the disclosed non-falsifiable vh/dvh mechanism and the found-in-testing `flex flex-col` bug are handled correctly). Remaining findings are hardening and a small residual-layout risk, none of which block. Ship-with-fixes at most; the dvh/top-10% interaction deserves a follow-up note.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: approve
